description:
memory.rs:296-301:

    let base = *BASE.get_or_init(|| {
        SystemTime::now()
            .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
            .map(|d| d.as_nanos() as u64)
            .unwrap_or(1_000_000_000)
    });

Duration::as_nanos() returns u128. The `as u64` cast silently truncates. cargo clippy -- -W clippy::pedantic flags this with cast_possible_truncation.

For SystemTime::now() vs UNIX_EPOCH the value fits in u64 until the year 2554 (u64::MAX nanoseconds since 1970 is roughly 584.5 years). The truncation will not fire in practice, BUT the idiom is still wrong: `as` casts that lose precision should be either:
  - Documented with a `#[allow(clippy::cast_possible_truncation)]` and a one-line comment saying "fits in u64 until year 2554",
  - Or written as `u64::try_from(d.as_nanos()).unwrap_or(1_000_000_000)`,
  - Or done at u128 width and only narrowed at the format! call site (`format!("{n:032x}")`).

The current line silently hides a truncation that future-proof code should not have. The realistic-demo-ids branch is already labeled "NOT A PRODUCTION PATTERN" in the docstring — a reader copying this for a real backend will inherit the silent truncation.

Same pattern in canonical jmap-mail-server/src/memory.rs:278 — propagation needed.
title: demo_next_id realistic mode: 'd.as_nanos() as u64' silently truncates u128 to u64
